items.title: TSG-01 in the treatment of chronic heart failure in patients with coronary artery disease: A prospective clinical phase IIa trial.
items.abstract: TSG-01, a novel agent dominated by secondary ginsenosides, may benefit chronic heart failure (CHF), yet its efficacy and safety in CHF patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) remain unclear. This phase IIa trial enrolled 85 CAD patients with NYHA III CHF (40-75 years), randomized to high-dose TSG-01 (n=29), low-dose TSG-01 (n=28), or placebo (n=28) for 12 weeks. Outcomes were evaluated in the intention-to-treat cohort (ITT, n=85) and an exploratory digoxin-free cohort (n=59). No significant between-group difference was found for the NYHA-based efficacy endpoint. In the ITT cohort, only low-dose TSG-01 significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) versus placebo; in the digoxin-free cohort, both doses yielded significant LVEF improvement. Diseases occurring the infectious and infective system, gastrointestinal system and the blood and lymphatic system are the common adverse events, with no significant difference between the 3 groups. Together, this study demonstrates that TSG-01 is well tolerated with similar adverse event profiles across groups, and confers potential cardiac benefits in digoxin-free patients, warranting further confirmatory studies. Registration: Clinicaltrials.gov, no. NCT04515290.

items.title: Blood-Pressure-Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum.
items.abstract: Treatment for lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of cardiovascular events among persons at high risk. Whether this benefit extends to those at lower risk remains unclear. We performed a meta-analysis of individual participant data from randomized trials comparing antihypertensive treatment (intervention) with placebo, an active comparator, or usual care (comparator). The primary outcome was the first occurrence of a major cardiovascular event (fatal or nonfatal stroke, fatal or nonfatal ischemic heart disease, or heart failure resulting in death or hospitalization; composite outcome). Safety was assessed in trials that compared antihypertensive treatment with placebo or usual care, according to three prespecified composite outcomes: cardiovascular or hemodynamic events (palpitations, bradycardia, or hypotension), adverse renal events, and neurovestibular or fall-associated events. Participants were grouped into deciles according to predicted 5-year risk of a major cardiovascular event (median, 12.3%; lowest decile, 27%). We included data from 51 trials and 357,440 participants - 169,042 in the intervention group and 188,398 in the comparator group. Over a median follow-up of 4.2 years, a major cardiovascular event occurred in 19,202 participants (11.4%) in the intervention group and in 24,398 (13.0%) in the comparator group. The overall estimated hazard ratio for a major cardiovascular event per 5-mm Hg reduction in systolic blood pressure was 0.90 (95% confidence interval, 0.88 to 0.92), with no evidence of variation across deciles. The absolute reduction in the 5-year cumulative risk of a major cardiovascular event was greater in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (2.6 vs. 0.4 percentage points), and the number needed to treat to prevent one major cardiovascular event over 5 years was lower in the highest decile than in the lowest decile (38 vs. 255). The incidence of a cardiovascular or hemodynamic event was 12.0 per 1000 person-years in the intervention group and 6.5 per 1000 person-years in the comparator group; the incidence of an adverse renal event was 3.3 and 2.2 per 1000 person-years, respectively; and the incidence of a neurovestibular or fall-associated event was 19.1 and 16.6 per 1000 person-years. The relative increase in the risk of each safety-outcome event with antihypertensive treatment as compared with placebo or usual care did not appear to vary across deciles. Blood-pressure lowering was associated with a decreased risk of major cardiovascular events across the risk spectrum, including a predicted 5-year risk below 4%. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation; PROSPERO registry number, CRD42018099283.).

items.title: A Decade of Evolving Pediatric Acute Cardiac Care Nursing Characteristics: Results From the Consortium of Congenital Cardiac Care-Measurement of Nursing Practice (C4-MNP).
items.abstract: Intensive care unit (ICU) nursing experience, education, and critical care certification have been linked to pediatric cardiovascular patient outcomes. While pediatric acute cardiac care is also complex, high-risk, and requires specialized nurses, little is known about nurse characteristics in this care area. To describe the evolving characteristics of pediatric cardiac nurses in non-ICU settings over 10 years and to compare these characteristics to established benchmarks. Aggregate data were collected from participating pediatric acute cardiac care units and inpatient units in 2016, 2022, and 2025. Benchmarks included the proportion of nurses with a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) or higher, ≤2 years of experience, and specialty pediatric certification. Descriptive statistics summarized percentages at the unit and aggregate levels and compared results to a 2015 baseline survey, subsequent time points, and the benchmark. The median of BSN-prepared nurses increased from 87% (2016) to 96% (2022/2025), with all units meeting the benchmark (2022). Nurses with ≤2 years of experience remained stable (median: 40% to 43%), with 1 unit meeting the benchmark (2025). Specialty certification declined from 44% (2016) to 19% (2025), with 3 units meeting the benchmark (2025). This is the first report describing the characteristics of pediatric cardiac nursing over a 10-year period. While education has increased to benchmark, vulnerabilities remain in experience and certification. Ongoing benchmarking and collaboration are needed to support nursing practice and ensure high-quality care for pediatric cardiac patients.

Pathologic Complete Response and Recurrence Rates After Neoadjuvant Systemic Therapy in Metaplastic Breast Cancer.
items.abstract: Metaplastic breast cancer (MpBC) is rare, often triple-negative, and has historically had lower systemic therapy response rates and inferior outcomes compared with other breast cancer subtypes. The addition of immunotherapy to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) has led to improved pathologic complete response (pCR) rates, event-free survival, and overall survival in patients with unselected triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). Whether or to what degree benefits of NAC with immunotherapy are seen in patients with MpBC is unknown. Eligible participants with nonmetastatic MpBC treated with preoperative therapy between January 2010 and June 2024 were ascertained from pathology and treatment records at the University of Pennsylvania. Two cohorts of patients were evaluated: (1) patients who received NAC and (2) patients who received NAC with immunotherapy (NACI). Objectives were to evaluate pCR and recurrence rates. Eighty-five individuals with MpBC and prior neoadjuvant therapy were identified, including 51 and 34 patients who received NAC and NACI, respectively. Rates of pCR were 17.6% with NAC and 26.5% with NACI (21.2% overall). No clinical factors were associated with pCR, including clinical stage or histopathologic subtype of MpBC. With a median follow-up of 29.6 months after surgery, distant metastatic disease developed in 52.9% and 17.6% of patients who received NAC and NACI, respectively. No patients with pCR developed distant metastatic disease. pCR rates in individuals with MpBC remain low despite the benefits of NACI seen in studies of unselected TNBC. Individuals with MpBC who experience pCR have favorable outcomes, underscoring the need to understand biomarkers of treatment response in these patients.

items.title: Optimizing Eculizumab and Ravulizumab Initiation in Myasthenia Gravis: Infection Risk, Vaccination Timing, and Antibiotic Prophylaxis.
items.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder characterized by fatigable muscle weakness and fluctuating symptoms. Complement component 5 inhibitor therapies (C5ITs) such as ravulizumab and eculizumab are rapidly acting treatments for generalized MG (gMG) but associated with an increased risk of meningococcal infection. As such, an ideal strategy for initiating C5IT requires effective mitigation of meningococcal infection risk that permits timely amelioration of disease burden. While C5ITs are approved for several indications, this review focuses on gMG. The available data on infection risk associated with eculizumab and ravulizumab are discussed, and practical approaches for starting these medications are presented. Previously, C5IT could be started 2 weeks after the initial doses of meningococcal vaccines. The 2024 updates to meningococcal vaccination policies in the United States extended the completion schedule from 2 months to 6 months and allowed for clinical judgment in initiating C5ITs earlier. In treating patients whose severity of gMG necessitates starting C5ITs before the 6-month vaccination schedule can be completed, clinicians need to consider several factors, including the risk of meningococcal infection, whether the expected reduction in disease burden and improvement in quality of life justify the infection risk, and the potential complications of prolonged antibiotic prophylaxis as an infection risk mitigation strategy. In our opinion, data used to support the change in vaccine schedule did not show a substantial difference in seroresponses. Since C5ITs are likely to remain an important treatment option for gMG, consideration of early vaccination after the diagnosis is recommended to minimize delays in the initiation of C5ITs. Clinical trial data suggest that risk of meningococcal infection in patients with gMG is low, particularly during the first 6 months after C5IT initiation. The evidence supporting the use of extended antibiotic prophylaxis in this patient population is currently scarce. However, clinicians must ensure that the patient is fully aware of the risk, the symptoms of meningococcal disease, and the need for prompt medical attention if those symptoms occur. By taking a comprehensive, individualized approach, clinicians can facilitate the safe and effective use of C5ITs in patients with gMG.

items.title: TCR Signal Strength and Eomes Shape CD8⁺ T Cell Fate Antitumor Immunity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) poses a persistent barrier to effective immunotherapy, in part due to the emergence of exhausted CD8⁺ T cells. Using a hydrodynamic, autochthonous HCC model based on Sleeping Beauty-mediated delivery of oncogenic drivers and defined OVA derived antigens, we could manipulate antigen affinity under physiological priming conditions. With this system, we examined how TCR signal strength and the transcription factor Eomesodermin (Eomes) shape CD8⁺ T cell fate in vivo. High affinity stimulation supported robust effector differentiation and the formation of tissue resident memory T cells (Trm), resulting in early tumor control. In contrast, low affinity stimulation induced elevated Eomes expression and favored rapid transition toward an exhausted (Tex) phenotype. Genetic repression of Eomes enhanced Trm differentiation in high affinity CD8⁺ T cells and delayed tumor relapse, whereas ectopic Eomes expression accelerated exhaustion and led to earlier tumor recurrence. Under low affinity conditions, Eomes deficiency increased the Trm to Tex ratio but remained insufficient to restore effective antitumor immunity, indicating that weak TCR engagement imposes constraints that cannot be overcome by Eomes loss alone. These findings reveal that the strength of TCR engagement shapes CD8⁺ T cell fate in HCC, while Eomes selectively biases this process toward exhaustion at the expense of effector and resident memory programs, ultimately influencing the durability of tumor control.

items.title: CCR2/5 antagonist with radiation and immunotherapy shows higher resectability for locally advanced pancreatic cancer and increased intratumoral CD8+CD137+ T cells.
items.abstract: Locally advanced pancreatic adenocarcinoma (LAPC) has a low resection rate (22%). In our prior phase II study, cancer vaccination (GVAX), pembrolizumab, SBRT and chemotherapy was associated with improved distant metastasis-free survival, but increased M2-like macrophages correlated with worse survival. In preclinical models, cysteine-cysteine chemokine receptors 2 (CCR2) and 5 (CCR5) blockade overcomes macrophage-driven resistance. We therefore initiated a phase I/II trial of nivolumab and BMS-813160 (CCR2/5 inhibitor) ± GVAX with FOLFIRINOX, SBRT, and surgery for LAPC. Primary endpoints were safety and changes in intratumoral CD137+CD8+ T cells which correlate with favorable survival. Twenty-two patients were treated; the remainder had disease progression during chemotherapy, withdrew consent, or did not meet eligibility prior to study treatment. In phase I (n=9), patients received nivolumab 480mg IV, GVAX 5x108 cells intradermal q4 weeks, and BMS-813160 150mg PO BID (DL1, n=3) or 300mg PO BID (DL2, n=6) with no dose limiting toxicities. In phase II (n=13), patients were randomized to nivolumab and BMS-813160 without (Arm A) or with (Arm B) GVAX; 3/5 patients (Arm A) and 8/11 patients (Arm B + DL2) achieved the primary immunologic endpoint. Fourteen patients had paired tumor biopsies with 13 showing >80% increase in CD137+CD8+ T cells meeting the primary immunology endpoint. Fourteen (64%) of 22 treated patients underwent R0/R1 resection which was numerically higher than historical LAPC data. In conclusion, adding nivolumab, BMS-813160, and GVAX to chemo-radiotherapy is tolerable and associated with favorable immunologic and clinical outcomes, though substantial attrition before study therapy limits definitive conclusions.

items.title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion.
items.abstract: Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4 + tumor cells, with CD8 + T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand-receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8 + T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8 + T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8 + T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8 + T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8 + T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4-GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

items.title: Efficacy of Bovine Lactoferrin in Chronic Hepatitis C: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Bovine lactoferrin (bLF), a glycoprotein with antiviral and immunomodulatory properties, has been investigated as a potential therapeutic agent. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy of bLF on virologic and biochemical outcomes in patients with chronic HCV infection. PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched from inception through November 5, 2024 (CRD42024621752). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing bLF with placebo or no treatment. Pooled analyses used a random-effects inverse-variance model. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², with exploratory subgroup analyses and meta-regression. Five randomized controlled trials were included, four contributing to quantitative analyses. No statistically significant differences were observed for virologic response (RR = 1.00, 95% CI: 0.74-1.36; I² = 31%), biochemical response (RR = 1.04, 95% CI: 0.71-1.53; I² = 0%), or sustained virologic response (RR = 1.06, 95% CI: 0.63-1.76; I² = 0%). Subgroup analyses and meta-regression identified no significant sources of heterogeneity. The available randomized evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit of bLF on virologic or biochemical responses. Further studies using contemporary treatment strategies and mechanistic endpoints are warranted.

items.title: Compound heterozygosity for I692del and V726A variants in MEFV leads to severe autoinflammation and elevated interleukin-18 (CHIVE-18).
items.abstract: We describe a severe MEFV -associated autoinflammatory disease, distinct from familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), and designate it CHIVE-18 syndrome (Compound Heterozygosity for I692del and V726A MEFV variants and Elevated IL-18). We present the clinical features and inflammatory signatures of 44 CHIVE-18 patients and 9 other patients with two MEFV variants including I692del. Clinical findings in CHIVE-18 patients often include transfusion-dependent anemia, arthritis, organomegaly, inflammatory bowel disease, failure to thrive, and less frequently cytokine storm, Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis, and neutrophilic dermatoses. Serum total and free IL-18 levels in CHIVE-18 patients were markedly elevated compared to those of healthy controls, classical FMF patients, and compound heterozygotes for I692del and a pathogenic MEFV variant other than V726A and were comparable to the previously described levels of patients with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome. Cultured U937 cells expressing the V726A/I692del double mutant exhibited significantly increased release of IL-1β, IL-18, and lactate dehydrogenase compared to the other FMF-associated mutants. Patients' myeloid cells showed enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation after stimulation with IFNγ. Despite having undetectable serum IL-1β, a previously reported CHIVE-18 patient with autoimmune hepatitis had in situ staining of a liver biopsy that showed high expression of IL-1β, TNFα, and IL-18, which localized to CD68+ tissue macrophages. CHIVE-18 patients usually require an IL-1 inhibitor and sometimes combination therapy with another biologic to control disease activity. In summary, CHIVE-18 is a distinct, severe disease that expands the spectrum of MEFV -associated autoinflammatory disorders and highlights genotype/phenotype complexity in compound heterozygous disorders.

items.title: Love, Sex, and Immunosuppression: A Sexual Health Overview for the Transplant Clinician.
items.abstract: Sexual health is a critical, yet often overlooked, aspect of comprehensive care for solid organ transplant recipients. While transplantation can restore overall health and quality of life, patients may continue to experience sexual dysfunction because of physiological, psychological, and pharmacological factors. Furthermore, transplant recipients remain at risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs), including HIV, human papillomavirus (HPV), syphilis, and others, with implications for both patient and graft outcomes. HPV-associated malignancies, particularly anal squamous cell carcinoma, occur at significantly higher rates in this population, highlighting the need for recommendations on targeted screening and vaccination. This review addresses the spectrum of sexual health issues across transplant populations-including liver, kidney, heart, and lung recipients-with practical guidance on sexual function, STI screening, and risk reduction strategies. We outline current evidence and recommendations for preexposure and postexposure prophylaxis against HIV and bacterial STIs, including the use of tenofovir-based preexposure prophylaxis and doxycycline postexposure prophylaxis. We also aim to highlight the role of immunization against HPV, hepatitis B, hepatitis A, and monkeypox virus, emphasizing safety, timing, and efficacy considerations in immunocompromised individuals. Despite growing awareness, implementation of routine sexual health assessment and STI prevention strategies remains inconsistent in transplant medicine. We call for greater integration of sexual health into transplant care pathways and identify key research priorities to optimize outcomes. Clinicians should feel empowered to initiate open conversations, advocate for vaccination and prophylaxis, and tailor care based on individualized risk. This comprehensive update offers practical tools and recommendations to improve sexual health in solid organ transplant recipients.

items.title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Hepatitis B and/or C Virus Infections among Medical Waste Handlers in Ethiopia: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Health systems around the world are severely impacted by hepatitis B Virus and hepatitis C Virus, particularly in low- and middle-income nations. These viruses are still more common in Ethiopia even with preventive efforts including the hepatitis B vaccine, universal precautions, and occupational safety procedures. There is little information available on their frequency and related variables among Ethiopian medical waste handlers. The purpose of this meta-analysis and systematic review was to ascertain the prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C in this population as well as its contributing factors. Different databases, including PubMed, Science Direct, Cochrane, Hinari, Google Scholar, grey literature, and articles from different university repository sites, were examined in order to locate available publications. Five studies with a total sample size of 1,211 participants were included in this systematic review and meta-analysis. The data was extracted and sorted using Microsoft Excel version 13 before being sent to STATA/MP 17.0 for analysis. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess each study's quality. The pooled prevalence of the hepatitis B and C virus was examined using a Der Simonian random-effects model with a 95% confidence interval. The Egger's test and I 2 were used to evaluate publication bias and heterogeneity. The possible cause of heterogeneity was assessed using both subgroup analysis and meta-regression. P-values less than 0.05 were considered statistically significant. The pooled prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C viruses among Ethiopian medical waste handlers was 13% (95% CI: 5-21%), according to the findings of this comprehensive study and meta-analysis. Significant heterogeneity is shown in the Galbraith plot, with I 2  = 96.21% (p < 0.001). The prevalence of hepatitis B and/or C viruses was 11.3%, according to studies conducted until the year 2020. However, studies included less than 260 participants found that the prevalence of the hepatitis B and/or C virus was 14.90%. This study found that having multiple sexual partners and prior exposure to sharp objects were associated with Hepatitis B Virus and/or Hepatitis C Virus infection among medical waste handlers. These findings highlight the role of behavioral and occupational factors in hepatitis transmission. Therefore, reducing infection risk requires promoting safe sexual practices and strengthening infection prevention and control measures in healthcare settings.

items.title: Dual Functional Cure in HBV/HIV-1 Co-infection: A Narrative Review for Critical Appraisal of Current Evidence and Conceptual Framework.
items.abstract: The syndemic of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1) affects millions of people worldwide. Each virus exacerbates the pathogenesis of the other, leading to accelerated liver disease and increased mortality. While combined antiretroviral therapy (cART) suppresses both viruses, it rarely achieves a functional cure, which is defined as sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) seroclearance for HBV and durable cART-free remission for HIV-1, due to persistent viral reservoirs (covalently closed circular DNA for HBV and integrated proviral DNA for HIV-1). Recent parallel advances in HBV and HIV-1 cure research have generated considerable interest in a "dual functional cure". In this review, we critically evaluate whether current evidence supports such a concept. We first summarize the epidemiology of HBV/HIV-1 coinfection, and then outline coinfection‑specific barriers and opportunities that distinguish a dual cure from a simple superposition of two single‑disease strategies. Next, we compare major cure strategies (interferon‑based, immune checkpoint blockade, Toll‑like receptor agonists, broadly neutralizing antibodies, gene editing, and latency targeting) in terms of evidence level in monoinfection versus coinfection, safety concerns, and translational barriers. Finally, we propose a sequential, personalized framework as a hypothesis‑generating tool, emphasizing that most steps remain extrapolations requiring dedicated coinfection trials. We conclude by defining actionable research priorities, including patient selection criteria, end point choices, and management of hepatitis flares.

items.title: mirCCC: Repression-aware graph learning for miRNA-mediated cell-cell communication inference.
items.abstract: Cell-cell communication analyses usually focus on protein ligands and receptors and therefore miss extracellular vesicle transfer of microRNAs, an important route of signalling in cancer. Here we show that microRNA-mediated communication can be inferred from standard single-cell RNA sequencing by detecting coordinated decreases in the expression of validated miRNA target genes. We developed mirCCC, a computational framework that estimates cell-specific microRNA activity, models cellular sending and receiving capacity for extracellular vesicle transfer, and learns microRNA-resolved communication graphs from transcriptomic data. In synthetic benchmarks with strong confounding signals, mirCCC improved whereas all comparison methods declined. Applied to a human colorectal cancer atlas, mirCCC recovered known colorectal cancer-associated microRNAs and identified stromal- and myeloid-to-epithelial communication converging on a plasticity program linked to TGF-β and Wnt/β-catenin signalling. These results provide a practical route for studying extracellular vesicle-mediated communication in existing single-cell atlases.

items.title: MitoVeritas: a dual-omics-informed AI framework for eliminating NUMT-derived artifacts in low-frequency mtDNA mutation detection.
items.abstract: Low-frequency mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations are promising biomarkers, yet nuclear-embedded mtDNA sequences (NUMTs) cause hard-to-eliminate false positives that largely evade consensus-based error correction, including Duplex Sequencing. We present MitoVeritas, a machine-learning framework that uses paired mtDNA-mtRNA data to define training labels and can then be applied to mtDNA data alone. Because genuine mtDNA mutations retain representation in mitochondrial transcripts whereas NUMT-derived variants usually do not, we built a benchmark from 96 hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients, reserving 81 for model development and 15 as an untouched hold-out set defined before model selection. Using 30 features in an XGBoost classifier, MitoVeritas identified 184 of 190 genuine mutations (96.8% sensitivity) and 213 of 223 NUMT-derived artifacts (95.5% specificity) in the hold-out patients. In an independent ovarian cancer patient-derived xenograft cohort, sensitivity was 99.6% and specificity 98.4%; because these labels follow the same dual-omics rules, this analysis tests cohort-level transfer rather than the labeling assumptions. A PacBio HiFi-derived benchmark, in which variant origin was assigned independently of mtRNA evidence, provided orthogonal ground truth, and MitoVeritas showed the most balanced sensitivity-specificity trade-off among the pipelines evaluated. In real-world datasets, it preserved 94.3% of mutations without NUMT support while substantially reducing NUMT-contaminated calls at 0.1%-1% variant allele frequency, and performance was maintained across the fresh-tissue, formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded, and cell-line datasets examined. As development used HCC samples exclusively, performance in normal tissues, other tumor types, and other sequencing workflows remains to be established. MitoVeritas is open-source and compatible with standard short-read sequencing data.

items.title: JMJD5 regulates metabolism by hydroxylating ISY1, and regulating the arginine methyltransferase PRMT6.
items.abstract: 2-Oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases (2OGDDs) couple molecular oxygen, 2-oxoglutarate, and Fe(II) to catalysis, allowing some family members to report on cellular metabolic state. Jumonji-C domain-containing protein 5 (JMJD5) is a 2OGDD linked to histone modification, DNA-damage repair and metabolism, and is reduced in hepatocellular carcinoma, where low expression correlates with poor survival. Here, we describe a signaling pathway in which JMJD5 hydroxylates arginine 3 of the spliceosome component ISY1. Hydroxylated ISY1 binds protein arginine N-methyltransferase 6 (PRMT6) and restrains its activity, and deleting PRMT6 reverses most of the proteomic, arginine-methylation and histone changes caused by JMJD5 loss. In a genetically engineered murine liver cancer model, Jmjd5 loss suppressed tumor growth and rewired one-carbon, amino acid and lipid metabolism, recapitulating the changes seen in human cells. The JMJD5-ISY1-PRMT6 axis clarifies controversies over JMJD5 function and identifies PRMT6 as a candidate target in JMJD5-low cancers.

items.title: Quantitative comparison of SPECT- and PET- based methods for treatment planning and dosimetry in Y-90 radioembolisation therapy.
items.abstract: Quantitative post-therapy imaging is essential for verifying administered activity and assessing dose distribution following Y-90 radioembolisation. This study compared large energy acceptance window Y-90 SPECT and PET for estimating implanted activity relative to the standard SIRTEX vial calibration method and evaluated their equivalence dosimetry. The retrospective Y-90 SPECT were acquired using protocols optimised for qualitative rather than quantitative imaging. The predictive accuracy of Tc-99​m MAA SPECT and compartmental models for pre-therapy dosimetry estimation was also investigated. A cohort of 28 patients treated with Y-90 resin microspheres underwent pre-therapy Tc-99​m MAA SPECT and post-therapy Y-90 SPECT and PET. The regional doses (tumour, perfused liver, and lungs) were calculated using the local deposition model. Equivalence between methods was assessed using the two one-sided tests. The Y-90 SPECT and PET measurements of implanted activity was on average -3 % ± 12 % and -5 % ± 13 %, of the SIRTEX calculated method. Tumoural doses derived from Y-90 SPECT and PET were statistically equal and equivalent (mean difference -1 %, SD ± 14 %), and perfused liver doses were equivalent within ±5 Gy (mean difference 2 Gy, SD 13 Gy). Despite statistical equivalence, a 14-42% variability in individual measurements remained. Tc-99​m MAA SPECT-predicted tumour doses showed closer agreement with PET doses than the partition model (4% vs 6%), while perfused liver and lung predictions were comparable. Although PET remains the current clinical reference standard, Y-90 SPECT provides clinically acceptable equivalence where PET is not available while supporting post-therapy verification and retrospective dosimetric analyses.
